text: Infrared inspection of this work has shown that the small magenta horseshoe-like shapes surrounding the legs of its central subject were originally flowers. 44 years after this work was painted, its artist created a second version of it that made more explicit a pair of white tables and the shadows they cast. Matthias Grunewald's Mocking of Christ likely inspired the blindfold worn by one of its subjects. John Russell once claimed that "there was painting in England before" this work, "and painting after it, and no one ... can confuse the two." Its left side features a ginger-haired figure perched atop a table, while on its right side, a patch of grass can be seen under the single limb of a figure with an elongated neck, large ear, and widely-opened mouth. Originally designed as a predella to a larger altarpiece, this work consists of a series of burnt-orange panels featuring distorted, elongated figures representing the Furies. FTP, name this 1944 triptych by Francis Bacon.

answer.canonical: Three Studies for Figures at the Base of a Crucifixion

text: He's not Vermeer, but this artist used the same model in his painting Christ in the House of Mary and Martha and a work that shows a boy carrying a melon standing next to the title woman. A figure in a blue sash holds up a mirror into which a naked woman looks in another painting by this artist, who also showed the god of wine surrounded by happy men in Los borrachos, or The Triumph of Bacchus. This artist of Old Woman Cooking Eggs and the Rokeby Venus also depicted himself wearing a red cross in a painting where Philip IV is reflected in a mirror and the Infanta Margarita is surrounded by her attendants. For 10 points, name this Spanish painter of Las Meninas.

answer.canonical: Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez

text: In one of this composer's operas, Ilia falls in love with a man who is later sacrificed to Neptune, named Idamonte. Lorenzo Da Ponte wrote the libretto for one of his operas, in which Guglielmo and Ferrando place a bet with Don Alfonso about the faithfulness of their fiancées. He also composed an opera in which the titular character's servant, Leporello, lists off a catalogue of his master's sexual conquests. In another opera by this composer of Cosi Fan Tutte, the Queen of the Night plots against Tamino, who wields the title instrument. For 10 points, name this composer of Don Giovanni, The Marriage of Figaro, and The Magic Flute.

text: The Self-portrait, found in Florence, is atypical of this artist's work, which is more accurately characterized by canvases like Plowing in the Nivernais and the collections at a namesake museum in Fontainebleau. Late in life this artist traveled to Scotland to paint Highland scenes, much like her friend and chief rival Edwin Landseer. [*] Studies for her most famous work, an enormous 1853 canvas, were made while she was disguised as a man at its namesake location. The first woman admitted to the French Legion of Honor, FTP, identify this painter of animal scenes, a native of Bordeaux who produced The Horse Fair.
